issues.description: The PersonService.savePerson method has different return types between the template and the solution. In the template PersonService.savePerson returns a Person (public Person savePerson(Person person)), which matches the problem statement that POST/PUT /persons should return the saved/updated person in the response body. In the solution PersonService.savePerson is declared void (public void savePerson(Person person)), but PersonResource in the solution calls personService.savePerson(person) and expects a Person to return in order to return it in the ResponseEntity. This mismatch will cause compilation errors and contradicts the API behavior described in the problem statement (POST/PUT should return the saved person).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the PersonService.savePerson method return a Person (like in the template and consistent with the API contract). Update the solution implementation to 'public Person savePerson(Person person)' and return the newly created or updated Person instance so PersonResource can return it in the ResponseEntity. Alternatively, if intentionally designed otherwise, adjust PersonResource to retrieve the Person to return (e.g., return the saved Person explicitly) so the service and controller signatures are consistent with the problem specification.
